content:
Carries the prescribed Unit 3 hands-on activity, and is the last working session before the final pitch.

CORE IDEA
A redesign is not a new coat of paint. It is deciding what the thing is for, and removing what does not serve that.

1. The object is a tech product — an app or a website. Your anchor's front door from Session 4, or a product everyone at the table uses.
2. All seven prompts, as a team, silent first. Same discipline as last session.
3. Eliminate carries this session. Look at the board — most abandonment reasons are about too much, not too little.
4. Produce something visible. A drawn screen, not a description.

learning_objectives.statement: The object is a tech product — an app or a website
All seven prompts, as a team, silent first

active_learning_components.desc: What survived your team's merge last session? What of yours was dropped, and were they right?
active_learning_components.rationale: Recall from memory, log closed, before any new input. Retrieval beats re-reading for retention.

active_learning_components.desc: Generates the evaluation criteria from the students' own experience rather than handing them a heuristics list.
Teams of four. One tech product: a member's anchor front door, or an app everyone uses. Write in one sentence what it is *for*.
Teams apply SCAMPER to redesign or enhance a tech product (e.g., a mobile app or website).
A3. Draw the redesigned screen or front door. Mark which SCAMPER prompt produced each change.
3 minutes, individual again. Hold the A3 up and name the prompt behind your favourite change.
Note the change you argued for that the team rejected.

early_finisher_extension: Redesign it again for a customer with a three-thousand-rupee phone and one gigabyte of data a month.
between_sessions: Bring every artefact you have made — all maps, grids, sketches — to Session 15.

forward_link.say: Auditing and redesigning a digital front door is the core of the local-discovery work in Semester III.
